risks.title: U.S.-China Trade and Tariff Tensions
risks.score_rationale: The risk is listed at the top of the Risk Factors section and describes concrete measures (Section 232/301 tariffs, IEEPA) with increases up to 100%. The language is alarming with recent escalation.

risks.title: Dependence on International Contract Manufacturers
risks.score_rationale: The document highlights reliance on foundries and subcontractors in Asia. The risk is repeated across multiple sections with strong language.

risks.title: Cyberattacks and IT System Failures
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned in Overall Business Operations with concerning language. Fundamental for a technology company and critical in 2025.

risks.title: Currency Fluctuations and Foreign Exchange Risk Management
risks.score_rationale: Recurring operational risk with measured language. Present every year, without notable worsening. Less critical than geopolitical risks but structural.

risks.title: Patent Sales and Non-Recurring Revenue
risks.score_rationale: The document explicitly mentions material fluctuations in revenue and gross margins related to patent licensing and sales. Direct impact on earnings predictability.

risks.title: Competition with Better-Funded Players
risks.score_rationale: The risk is clearly stated with references to competitors having significantly more resources. In a technology-intensive sector, this threatens innovation capacity.

risks.title: Geopolitical Instability in Europe and the Middle East
risks.score_rationale: The Ukraine-Russia conflict and Middle East tensions are cited as sources of volatility. The link to energy and logistics supply chains is explicit.

ai_positioning.summary: Lattice recognizes AI as a major catalyst. The company explicitly mentions AI in its secular trends, Edge AI applications, and its use in AI-optimized servers, face detection, image recognition, and video analytics. However, AI is not presented as a core strategic pillar in the 10-K report.
evidence: AI is driving shorter design cycles, allowing less time to integrate auxiliary functions
Edge AI applications including device usage in AI-optimized servers in data centers, AI-enabled PCs, and AI-enabled robotics and ADAS systems
Lattice devices support applications like face detection, image recognition, human-machine interface (HMI), and video analytics
With the increase in artificial intelligence (AI) and a multitude of applications at the network edge
